text:
4. [RARC.5.6.5] Hands the change to the network, which propagates it
   through its alpha and beta memories and populates or updates the agenda.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__neg_facts_frame
idris.note: And its `no` facts only through the kinds its `no` patterns name.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule_frame
idris.note: Re-propagation of a rule that does not read the changed kind is the identity on its table.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__tuples_frame
idris.note: A rule's match tuples depend on working memory only through the kinds it matches.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__no_tokens
idris.note: One empty table per rule.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__no_tokens_nth
idris.note: The r-th empty table exists for every rule index.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__table_frame
idris.note: After a change of kind k, a rule that does not read k keeps its table, still settled.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__neg_facts_frame_pred
idris.note: Negated-pattern facts over kinds outside the change are unchanged.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule_frame_pred
idris.note: A rule reading no kind of the change keeps its propagation.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__table_frame_pred
idris.note: A rule reading no kind of the change keeps its table: frame and settledness.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__tuples_frame_pred
idris.note: Tuples over kinds outside the change are unchanged.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__show_idris
idris.note: A state as an Idris expression, so a run's states can be pasted back as literals for the witness proofs.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_5__state
idris.note: The engine state Rete maintains: working memory and one token table per rule -- the agenda, populated and updated by propagation.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__any
idris.note: Structural-recursion list helper of the fire-loop model, defined here rather than taken from `Foldable` so that proofs unfold it; named under the propagation clause it serves. any.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__concat_map
idris.note: Structural-recursion list helper of the fire-loop model, defined here rather than taken from `Foldable` so that proofs unfold it; named under the propagation clause it serves. concatMap.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__elem
idris.note: Structural-recursion list helper of the fire-loop model, defined here rather than taken from `Foldable` so that proofs unfold it; named under the propagation clause it serves. elem.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__find
idris.note: Structural-recursion list helper of the fire-loop model, defined here rather than taken from `Foldable` so that proofs unfold it; named under the propagation clause it serves. find.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__init_state
idris.note: The initial state: the input working memory with every rule's tokens propagated from empty tables.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__nth
idris.note: Structural-recursion list helper of the fire-loop model, defined here rather than taken from `Foldable` so that proofs unfold it; named under the propagation clause it serves. Indexing, `Nothing` past the end.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule
idris.note: Re-propagate one rule after a working-memory change; factored through `rarc_5_6_5__prop_with` so it provably depends on working memory only through the kinds the rule reads.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_with
idris.note: Re-propagate one rule from its current match tuples and the facts its `no` patterns see: keep the tokens that still match (refreshing their blocking), drop the rest, append the new matches.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__propagate
idris.note: Re-propagate every rule.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__set_at
idris.note: Structural-recursion list helper of the fire-loop model, defined here rather than taken from `Foldable` so that proofs unfold it; named under the propagation clause it serves. Apply a function at one position.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__init_tms
idris.note: The initial state: the core's, with an empty table.

idris.name: iret_7_7__view
idris.note: The recompute the incremental network is proved to agree with: node by node, from the nil token, over working memory.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__agree_after_history
idris.note: THE TRANSFER OF CONTENT, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network, every terminal holds exactly the unblocked matches FireLoop's recompute gives the rule its chain lowers to. Order and flags are part two.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__recompute_agrees
idris.note: The two recomputes are one: the network's and Rete/FireLoop.idr's agree on every chain and working memory.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__terminal_agrees
idris.note: UNDER THE VIEW every terminal holds, as a set, exactly the unblocked matches of the rule its chain lowers to -- what Rete/FireLoop.idr's table holds with `blocked` clear.

idris.name: iret_7_6__recompute_after_history_4
idris.note: THE VIEW THEOREM WITH FOUR-VALUED TESTS: after any history every alpha memory and every terminal of the loaded four-valued network is the recompute over working memory. The view theorem is over any relation, so this is its instance; the lemmas beside it say the relations are the clauses'.

idris.name: iret_7_9_2__live_rejected
idris.note: Read off the recompute: a NOT node passes a prefix only with zero blockers.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_5__recomputed
idris.note: What the view says of an engine: every alpha memory is its schema's admitted facts, and every terminal holds exactly its chain's recompute over working memory, without duplicates.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__recompute_after_history
idris.note: THE VIEW THEOREM, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network -- every input pumped, in order [LFST.9.2.1] -- incremental propagation has left every alpha memory and every terminal exactly as the recompute over working memory would. Content only: the order theorem of [LDET.5.5] / [LDET.5.9] is the next increment.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__view_recomputed
idris.note: Under the view every terminal holds exactly its chain's recompute, without duplicates.

idris.name: iret_11_3__fires_the_match_count
idris.note: THE COUNT: under the view, the activations of every chain are as many as its matches, so the pump's firings are the number of distinct matches, summed over the rules.

idris.name: iret_11_3__match_count_from
idris.note: A terminal populated by propagation holds its recompute once, so its activations are as many as its matches.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__match_count
idris.note: What Rete propagates, counted: the recompute of every chain over the working memory it was handed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__view_distinct
idris.note: The recompute of a distinct front over distinct working memory is distinct.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__view_live
idris.note: The recompute of live tokens is live.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule_settled_id
idris.note: A settled table re-propagated over the same memory is itself: every token kept, nothing added, no refresh changes a token.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule_shrink_compose
idris.note: PROPAGATION AFTER SUCCESSIVE RETRACTIONS COMPOSES: a table settled under a memory, propagated over a sub-memory and then over a sub-memory of that, is the table propagated over the last once -- neither propagation adds a match, both keep the same survivors in place, and refreshing along a shrink composes because a retraction only ever releases a `no` pattern. What lets a cascade retract one fact at a time and end where the batch does.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__propagate_settled_id
idris.note: The tables of a well-formed state re-propagated over its memory are themselves: propagation is idempotent on a settled state.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__propagate_shrink_compose
idris.note: The tables of a well-formed state, propagated over a sub-memory and then over a sub-memory of that, are the tables propagated over the last once.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__zip_prop_settled_id
idris.note: Rule by rule.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__zip_prop_shrink_compose
idris.note: Rule by rule.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer_tms
idris.note: THE TRANSFER THEOREM WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE: run on one history from the loaded network and from FireLoopTms's empty state under the program the network lowers to, the two engines reach one working memory and one dependency table, and each table's unblocked tokens are the terminal's activations, in order and with their flags. Every theorem stated over FireLoopTms's run -- Rete/TmsRun.idr, Lcyc/TmsTermination.idr, Rete/PumpBoundary.idr -- is a theorem about the spec's network.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__transfer
idris.note: THE TRANSFER THEOREM: run on one history from the loaded network and from FireLoop's empty state under the program the network lowers to, the two engines reach one working memory, and each table's unblocked tokens are its terminal's activations, in order and with their flags. Against the plain pipeline, inputs without Rete/PumpBoundary.idr's TMS phase and without the clock; Rete/NetworkTmsTransfer.idr carries the phase and Rete/NetworkTtl.idr the clock, on this agreement.

idris.name: Rlow_4_2_1__agree
idris.note: THE NETWORK AND FIRELOOP AGREE: one working memory; each rule the lowering of its chain; each table's unblocked tokens its terminal's activations, in order and with their flags; both sides well-formed.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__change_agree
idris.note: THE AGREEMENT SURVIVES A CHANGE OF WORKING MEMORY: given the network after the change, ordered; FireLoop's state after one propagation, well-formed; the shapes kept; and the flags persisting -- the two agree again.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__tables_agree_step
idris.note: Tables agree with the new terminals after a propagation, rule by rule.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_5__tables_well
idris.note: Every table of a FireLoop state well-formed and settled against its rule.

idris.name: Rarc_5_6_5__well
idris.note: A WELL-FORMED FIRELOOP STATE: working memory distinct, ids unique, every table sorted, live and settled.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__init_table_well
idris.note: A rule's first table over empty working memory is well-formed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__init_tables_well
idris.note: Every rule's first table over empty working memory is well-formed and settled.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__init_well
idris.note: THE INITIAL STATE over empty working memory is well-formed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__propagate_well_grow
idris.note: One propagation after a fact enters keeps every table well-formed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__propagate_well_shrink
idris.note: One propagation after a fact leaves keeps every table well-formed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_after_history
idris.note: FIRELOOP'S STATE AFTER ANY HISTORY -- inputs applied without the TMS phase, each pumped -- is well-formed: every table in the key's order.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_assert
idris.note: An assert that changes working memory keeps the state well-formed, whichever shape it takes.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_grow
idris.note: A FRESH FACT APPENDED to a base contained in working memory keeps the state well-formed: the two working-memory invariants, and every table.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_shrink
idris.note: A FACT REMOVED keeps the state well-formed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__init_tms_inv
idris.note: The initial state satisfies the run invariant: the core's initial invariant, unique input ids, and an empty table.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__state_inj
idris.note: Constructor injectivity for the core state.
